Class InMemoryClientActivityDetector

java.lang.Object
edu.ucsb.cs.taapply.concurrency.InMemoryClientActivityDetector
All Implemented Interfaces:
ClientActivityDetector
public class InMemoryClientActivityDetector extends Object implements ClientActivityDetector
A ClientActivityDetector that keeps what it has seen in memory: for each resource key and client, when it arrived, when it was last seen and who it is.

The clock and the window are given to the constructor, so that tests run in no time with a clock they control. Every record(String, String, ClientIdentity) also forgets everything older than the window, on every resource, so the state stays as small as the activity of the last window.

One server only. A second server process would have a state of its own and the two would not see each other's clients. The application runs as one instance. If that changes, the state moves to the database behind this same interface.

    • leave

      public void leave(String resourceKey, String clientId)
      Description copied from interface: ClientActivityDetector
      Notes that this client has gone (issue #284): its tab or window was closed or left. It stops counting at once, instead of when the window has passed. Delivery of such a goodbye is not guaranteed, so the window stays as the fallback. A client that was not recorded is no change.
      Specified by:
      leave in interface ClientActivityDetector

    • arrival

      public Arrival arrival(String resourceKey, String clientId)
      Description copied from interface: ClientActivityDetector
      When this client arrived, as against the others active on the resource: see Arrival. A caller who has not been recorded is told it did not arrive last, and at time zero.
      Specified by:
      arrival in interface ClientActivityDetector

    • othersActive

      public List<OtherClient> othersActive(String resourceKey, String clientId)
      Description copied from interface: ClientActivityDetector
      The other people active on the resource within the window, one for each person, in order of label. A person is marked OtherClient.samePerson() if they are the same person as the caller, which means the caller has another tab or window open. The caller's own client is never among them. A caller who has not been recorded is nobody's same person.
      Specified by:
      othersActive in interface ClientActivityDetector
